evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Benjamin Diokno would lead the Marcos economic team as finance secretary, Arsenio Balisacan would return as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla would replace Diokno at the BSP.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key figures in Philippine President Marcos' administration
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Benjamin Diokno would lead the Marcos economic team as finance secretary, Arsenio Balisacan would return as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla would replace Diokno at the BSP.
evidence.source_locator: factbox entries for Diokno, Balisacan, and Medalla
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent wire, though the page is syndicated through MarketScreener.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; appointments were announced before Marcos was sworn in.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because these were his cabinet/economic-team selections.
contrary_evidence: Experienced appointments do not by themselves prove better execution or coordination.

evidence.claim: Marcos's first EO reorganized the Office of the President, abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, and said the administration sought simplicity, economy, and efficiency in the bureaucracy.
evidence.title: Executive Order No. 1
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's first EO reorganized the Office of the President, abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and the Office of the Cabinet Secretary, and said the administration sought simplicity, economy, and efficiency in the bureaucracy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary legal text signed by the president on his first day in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as a signed executive action.
contrary_evidence: Abolishing PACC can be read as streamlining, but also as reducing a specialized anti-corruption channel, so the net effect is ambiguous.

evidence.claim: Marcos presented the eight-point socioeconomic agenda to investors, saying it would address inflation and food security in the near term and jobs, infrastructure, human capital, digitalization, innovation, and livable communities over the medium term.
evidence.title: Road to progress: PBBM touts eight-point socio-economic agenda before US investors, biz leaders
evidence.excerpt: Marcos presented the eight-point socioeconomic agenda to investors, saying it would address inflation and food security in the near term and jobs, infrastructure, human capital, digitalization, innovation, and livable communities over the medium term.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted summary of the agenda
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release summarizing the president's own public presentation to investors.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because it is his own public articulation of the governing program.
contrary_evidence: Investor-facing rhetoric can overstate readiness and does not itself prove implementation.

evidence.claim: Marcos led the oath-taking of reappointed and ad interim cabinet members including Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, Alfredo Pascual, Renato Solidum Jr., Raphael Lotilla, and others.
evidence.title: PBBM leads oath-taking of Cabinet members in Malacañang
evidence.excerpt: Marcos led the oath-taking of reappointed and ad interim cabinet members including Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, Alfredo Pascual, Renato Solidum Jr., Raphael Lotilla, and others.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential release listing the actual appointees sworn into office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as the appointing authority.
contrary_evidence: Cabinet swearing-in does not itself prove effective coordination or delivery.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration said it had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to attract more domestic and foreign investment and make PPPs more attractive.
evidence.title: Marcos admin streamlines private sector participation processes to encourage investments
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration said it had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to attract more domestic and foreign investment and make PPPs more attractive.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official finance-ministry release describing enacted or operationalized investment reforms and their intended purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partially attributable to Marcos; some reforms were inherited or legislated earlier, but the administration is claiming operational ownership and sequencing.
contrary_evidence: Some of the enabling laws were passed before Marcos took office, so not all credit belongs to him.
Claims about improved investor response are forward-looking rather than outcome proof.

evidence.claim: The IMF said the new administration had a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but still faced three challenges: choosing the right policy mix for recovery and price stability, building fiscal buffers, and raising long-term growth.
evidence.title: Philippines: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said the new administration had a blueprint for an inclusive, sustainable, and green recovery, but still faced three challenges: choosing the right policy mix for recovery and price stability, building fiscal buffers, and raising long-term growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF country report with a clear summary of the administration's stated blueprint and macro tasks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Marcos's administration because the report describes its own blueprint and policy challenge set.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also implies the blueprint was still at the challenge-setting stage rather than proven execution.

evidence.claim: Government agencies had used 94% of the P4.01 trillion in Notices of Cash Allocation issued in the first 11 months of 2022, leaving P257.94 billion unused, up from 91% a year earlier.
evidence.title: Gov’t agencies’ cash usage hits 94% at end of Nov.
evidence.excerpt: Government agencies had used 94% of the P4.01 trillion in Notices of Cash Allocation issued in the first 11 months of 2022, leaving P257.94 billion unused, up from 91% a year earlier.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent business reporting citing DBM data, with explicit figures and comparison to the prior year.
evidence.period_fit: In-period; late-2022 execution metric for the Marcos administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos through administration-level spending control, but also affected by inherited budget processes and election-ban timing.
contrary_evidence: This is a cash-utilization measure, not a direct output or welfare outcome measure.
It does not isolate Marcos-specific agency performance from pre-existing spending momentum.

evidence.claim: In MIMAROPA, 24.8% of families were beneficiaries of 4Ps, 12.1% received AICS, and 84.8% had at least one member/dependent/beneficiary of PhilHealth in 2022.
evidence.title: Highlights of the 2022 Annual Poverty Indicators Survey: Social Protection Programs
evidence.publisher: Philippine Statistics Authority, MIMAROPA regional office
evidence.excerpt: In MIMAROPA, 24.8% of families were beneficiaries of 4Ps, 12.1% received AICS, and 84.8% had at least one member/dependent/beneficiary of PhilHealth in 2022.
evidence.source_locator: social assistance and PhilHealth sections in the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official PSA regional APIS release grounded in household survey data and reporting multiple program participation rates.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 reporting on 2022 household survey data.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: the figures reflect program reach under the Marcos period, but the article does not isolate his personal contribution from inherited program design and regional administration.
contrary_evidence: Regional reach is not the same as quality or effectiveness of delivery.
The data are regional and do not show whether Marcos personally improved access beyond inherited systems.

evidence.claim: PSA reported that 11 of 18 regions recorded statistically significant decreases in family poverty incidence in 2023 from 2021, while some regions saw increases or only non-significant downtrends.
evidence.title: 11 out of 18 Regions Recorded Significant Decreases in Poverty Incidence in 2023
evidence.excerpt: PSA reported that 11 of 18 regions recorded statistically significant decreases in family poverty incidence in 2023 from 2021, while some regions saw increases or only non-significant downtrends.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National statistics release with explicit regional poverty comparisons and significance language.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2024 regional follow-through on the 2022-2023 trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Marcos-era macro and social-policy choices, but also affected by inherited recovery patterns and regional heterogeneity.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2023 comparison against 2021, not a direct 2022 administration-only effect.
Some regions worsened, so the regional picture is mixed.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
